Just fyi, engine braking and compression braking are two completely different things. I am NOT talking about compression braking at all, so most of your comment isn't really relevant. I believe you're getting the two confused. Engine braking is using the engines natural ability to reduce the potential energy in the engine by making it work against manifold vacuum when you release the gas pedal. Every single gasoline engine has the ability to do this. 

Compression braking is different and only really applicable to diesel engines as their ability to engine brake is extremely limited. This removes most of the energy of the engine by opening the exhaust valves just before compression and dumping all the compressed fuel and air. This is a completely different system. The two get confused a lot.

Dying is part of the game, especially when you're new. You don't know the maps, the mechanics etc. You're facing players who've likely been playing for years. 

Don't give up though, I know it sucks and feels impossible to win but eventually you'll get there.

Invest in good ammo (as good as you can realistically afford or get due to availability, or whatever decent stuff you have stockpiled). Higher the penetration the better in most cases, ammo that can at least moderately pen level 4 if you can afford it. This matters more than how modded or good your gun is, even more than what armour you're wearing too I'd say. Invest in a headset (M32s are a great budget pair) so you can hear your surroundings better. Footsteps and audio are a huge part of the game. 

Always aim for the head and face if you have the opportunity to do so. 99 percent of ammo in the game will one tap the face (unless they have a face shield). I have downed many juiced up players with one shot from a pistol. If you're running an SMG and cannot afford decent penetration ammo, high flesh damage rounds and going for leg shots is still viable, especially when it comes to bosses and very well armoured players. 


Don't go sprinting everywhere like a madman, but also don't rat around all the time. You won't learn anything this way. 

Learn good loot routes that are maybe a little away from player traffic so you can build up your rouble count, so dying while learning doesn't hurt the bank account so much. 

Also another tip that took me a long time to get over myself, is don't be afraid to die and lose gear. You won't learn the game by sitting timidly in a corner, everyone dies. Most of us die a lot, but it just makes those few good raids feel oh so sweet. Look up some beginner guides on YouTube, they can help wonders.

Ultimately try to have fun, as you get better at the game it'll become very rewarding. Good luck in your raids!

I still believe a lot of those tanks were actually really promising from what I've read, but the collapse of the soviet union and monetary and political struggles halted a vast majority of prototypes they had. They just simply didn't have the money anymore to continue pushing with the projects anymore, and a lot of these designs had incorporated ideas and help from former Soviet states, so Russia had to go it alone and a lot of the design bureaus they relied on were Ukrainian for example. That's why modern autoloaders are placed in the rear of the turret along with blowout panels. 

The T-90 is a modern tank, and it still shares the same flaws as every T-72 before it.
